approvalRequirements: Own or lease a battery-electric or plug-in hybrid vehicle
Maintain an eligible Braintree residential electric account used for vehicle charging
Enroll the vehicle in the Charge & Save managed-charging program
Purchase and install qualifying Level 2 charging equipment
Submit the rebate claim with equipment and electrician expense documentation
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The rebate is rules-based for eligible residential customers who enroll, install qualifying Level 2 charging, and document eligible costs; routine claim verification remains required.
reviews.evidenceText: The current guide requires a Braintree residential account, an owned or leased plug-in vehicle, Charge & Save enrollment, qualifying Level 2 installation, and documented eligible expenses. The rebate is the lesser of $250 or eligible costs.

approvalRequirements: Be a new business tenant with an agreed lease at an eligible Santa Clara premises served by Silicon Valley Power
Enroll in Bright Start and complete the program energy assessment
Obtain landlord and tenant agreement on the proposed improvements
Install program-approved qualifying efficiency measures
Complete implementation review before incentive processing
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program provides enhanced rebates through a defined assessment and implementation process, so an eligible project is likely to receive the incentive after agreed measures are installed and approved.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Bright Start description requires a Santa Clara lease, program signup, an energy assessment, landlord and tenant agreement, implementation, and program approval. The page supports lighting and HVAC improvements and an assessment, but not the target low-flow-fixture mapping.

approvalRequirements: Use an approved contractor and obtain a qualifying project proposal
Register the home with TVA and obtain the required site identification
Submit the proposal and site identification before loan processing
Pass lender credit and financing review and execute loan documents before installation
Complete installation and pass the Bristol Tennessee Electric Service inspection before contractor payment
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Qualifying improvements can be financed, but award depends on credit approval, executed financing documents, eligible contractor work, and final inspection.
reviews.evidenceText: The current program requires an approved contractor proposal, TVA registration, financing qualification and signed documents before work, followed by a utility inspection before the installer is paid.

approvalRequirements: Maintain an eligible Brownsville Public Utilities Board account for the affected service
Use a qualifying measure and satisfy its technical and customer-class rules
Contact the program before installation when the measure requires advance qualification
Submit the current application within the measure-specific deadline
Provide invoices, equipment documentation, contractor or permit records, and any required inspection access
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The rebates are prescriptive and generally likely for eligible customers who meet measure rules, file within the required period, and pass document or field verification, subject to available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Current program pages require an eligible BPUB account, a complete and timely application, qualifying equipment, invoices and technical documents, and verification. HVAC projects require advance contact and may require permits, sizing documentation, and inspection.

approvalRequirements: Own a nonresidential building in Bryan Texas Utilities territory on an eligible commercial or industrial rate
Contact the program administrator to confirm project qualification
Complete an eligible project that demonstrates at least a 20 percent demand reduction
Finish the project within the applicable fiscal-year period
Submit before-and-after photographs, itemized invoices, and supporting savings documentation
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Supported commercial efficiency projects have a defined incentive formula and are likely to be paid after qualification and documentation, but the utility verifies demand reduction and eligibility.
reviews.evidenceText: The current SmartBUSINESS page requires an eligible nonresidential owner and rate, administrator qualification, at least 20 percent demand reduction, same-year completion, photographs, and invoices. It expressly says insulation does not qualify.

approvalRequirements: Own an eligible permanent single-family or multifamily dwelling in Bryan Texas Utilities territory
Have qualifying electric central heating and cooling service where required
Complete an eligible insulation or other listed SmartHOME project during the current fiscal year
Submit the application with invoices and before-and-after photographs
Allow a pre-installation or post-installation inspection if requested
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current program states that each qualifying project receives a percentage incentive, so payment is near-guaranteed after eligibility and documentation are verified.
reviews.evidenceText: The current SmartHOME page lists qualifying insulation measures and requires an eligible owner, current-year work, invoices, and before-and-after photographs. It states that each qualifying project receives an incentive, subject to program rules and inspection.

approvalRequirements: Meet Building Operator Certification course eligibility requirements
Operate a qualifying Santa Clara facility receiving Silicon Valley Power service
Obtain management approval and commit to completing the selected course
Submit a scholarship application for a specified class before attendance
Complete the course and provide documentation for reimbursement of the remaining eligible tuition
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Scholarships are limited and selected on a first-come basis, with reimbursement contingent on course completion; the benefit is not an equipment retrofit award.
reviews.evidenceText: The current scholarship page requires an eligible Santa Clara facility operator, management approval, course commitment, and application. A tuition discount is followed by reimbursement after completion. The official benefit concerns training, not EV chargers or low-flow fixtures.

approvalRequirements: Have an existing building automation or energy management system controlling eligible HVAC equipment
Submit the Building Optimization application and project plan before implementation or purchase
Receive Silicon Valley Power preapproval before starting the proposed optimization work
Complete assessment, implementation, commissioning, and required savings documentation
Pass post-installation inspection and participate in required savings verification
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The utility retains sole discretion over preapproval and verifies implementation and savings, so a technically eligible project has a possible rather than automatic award path.
reviews.evidenceText: The current application requires preapproval, optimization of existing HVAC controls, commissioning, inspection, and multi-year savings verification. It excludes new control systems and major expansions, so the target mappings to new BAS or EMS equipment and unrelated water measures require correction.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Burbank business customer
Install a qualifying catalog or custom energy-efficiency measure
Submit a complete rebate packet within four months after project completion
Provide project descriptions, before-and-after photographs, savings calculations where applicable, invoices, specifications, permits, and tax documentation
Allow Burbank Water and Power to inspect and verify the project before payment
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Catalog and custom incentives follow published formulas and are likely after a complete, timely submission and verification, subject to program funding and caps.
reviews.evidenceText: The current business-rebate page requires eligible completed measures, a packet filed within four months, itemized invoices, technical and savings documentation, permits and photographs, with inspection before payment when requested.

approvalRequirements: Have the authorized property representative notify Burbank Water and Power in writing before construction
Register the project for LEED certification and obtain the applicable City building permit
Complete the project and earn an eligible LEED certification level
Submit certification acceptance, the incentive application, and required tax documentation
Receive Burbank Water and Power review and acceptance of the completed certification package
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The incentive uses fixed amounts by certification level and is likely once required advance notice, registration, permitting, certification, and final documentation are satisfied.
reviews.evidenceText: The current LEED incentive page requires written notice before construction, proof of LEED registration and City permitting, then final certification acceptance, an application, and tax documentation for review.

approvalRequirements: Maintain an eligible Burbank Water and Power residential account
Purchase and install a currently qualifying product or measure
Submit the current rebate application with receipts, model or product documentation, and any required photographs
Obtain required permits and final inspection for measures that require them
Meet the measure-specific filing deadline and participation conditions, including EV time-of-use requirements where applicable
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The residential rebates are generally prescriptive and likely after a complete claim, but measure-specific documentation, deadlines, permits, and available funds still control payment.
reviews.evidenceText: Current pages direct residential customers to purchase and install qualifying products and submit complete documentation. EV charging claims require an active account, qualifying Level 2 equipment, licensed installation, permits, final inspection, timely filing, and time-of-use participation.

approvalRequirements: Maintain an eligible Burbank Water and Power nonresidential account
Deploy qualifying new listed charging equipment through a licensed contractor
Meet networking, load-management, permitting, and installation requirements applicable to the charger type
Obtain the final City permit and submit the application within six months
Provide invoices, equipment records, photographs, tax documentation, and inspection access and maintain the equipment for the required operating period
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The commercial charging rebate is prescriptive and likely for compliant installations with a timely, complete claim, though awards remain first-come and subject to available funding and inspection.
reviews.evidenceText: The current program requires an eligible nonresidential account, qualifying listed charging equipment, licensed installation, permits and final inspection, a claim within six months, invoices and photographs, and continued operation. Funding is first-come and limited.

approvalRequirements: Have the authorized property representative notify Burbank Water and Power in writing before construction
Register the project for LEED certification and obtain the applicable City building permit
Complete the project and earn an eligible LEED certification level
Submit certification acceptance, the incentive application, and required tax documentation
Receive Burbank Water and Power review and acceptance of the completed certification package
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The incentive uses fixed amounts by certification level and is likely once required advance notice, registration, permitting, certification, and final documentation are satisfied.
reviews.evidenceText: The current LEED incentive page requires written notice before construction, proof of LEED registration and City permitting, then final certification acceptance, an application, and tax documentation for review.

approvalRequirements: Be a Burlington Electric Department commercial customer at the project site
Select qualifying equipment or an eligible custom, renovation, or new-construction efficiency project
Contact Energy Services early for custom or construction projects and obtain any required project review before commitment
Provide equipment specifications, invoices, calculations, permits, and other measure-specific documentation
Complete installation and allow utility verification before final incentive processing
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Commercial incentives are generally available to eligible BED customers through prescriptive or custom paths, with award likely after measure qualification and verification.
reviews.evidenceText: Current BED pages make efficiency services available to commercial customers, direct custom and construction projects to early Energy Services review, and require qualifying equipment and project documentation. Some prescriptive refrigeration incentives are handled at purchase.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible small or medium Burlington Electric Department business with an active account
Demonstrate the required history of timely utility payments and satisfy credit and disclosure requirements
Provide property-owner permission, mortgage or lien information, and a lease term extending beyond the loan when applicable
Submit an acceptable contractor scope of work and execute the financing agreement before work begins
Complete the project and pass Burlington Electric Department inspection before funds are disbursed
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Financing is available for approved projects but depends on account history, underwriting, property and lien conditions, executed documents, and successful inspection.
reviews.evidenceText: The current on-bill financing page requires an active eligible business account, timely payment history, property and lien documentation, an accepted contractor scope, signed loan documents before work, and successful final inspection.

approvalRequirements: Maintain an eligible Burlington Electric Department residential account
Purchase or install a currently qualifying new product or measure
Submit the online rebate form within the measure-specific deadline
Provide invoices, product or contractor documentation, permits, and other required proof
Obtain advance approval for measures that specifically require it and allow verification or inspection
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Most listed residential rebates are prescriptive and likely after timely filing and documentation, although measure caps, permits, verification, and specific preapproval rules still apply.
reviews.evidenceText: The current rebate form lists 2026 residential offers and requires an account number, qualifying products, invoices and measure-specific documentation. Many claims have short filing deadlines and may be capped as a percentage of installed cost.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible New Hampshire for-profit or nonprofit business applicant
Request at least the program minimum financing amount for eligible energy-saving uses
Provide an independent third-party energy audit supporting the proposed project
Demonstrate adequate ability to repay and provide complete underwriting documentation
Receive New Hampshire Business Finance Authority staff and board approval
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The loan is not an entitlement; approval depends on project eligibility, minimum size, repayment capacity, underwriting, and formal staff and board action.
reviews.evidenceText: The current program requires at least $100,000 in financing, an energy-saving business purpose, a third-party energy audit, ability to repay, complete underwriting, and approval by staff and the authority board.

approvalRequirements: Be a business customer of a participating South Dakota Bright Energy Solutions utility
Use the current utility-specific application for an eligible business measure
Meet the applicable equipment, efficiency, installation, and customer requirements
Obtain preapproval before custom efficiency or custom electrification work
Submit invoices, equipment records, savings calculations, and other form-specific documentation
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Prescriptive rebates are generally likely for qualifying customers and equipment, while custom projects require advance approval and savings review.
reviews.evidenceText: The current directory lists 12 participating South Dakota utilities, not 11. Member pages provide utility-specific business rebate forms, and custom efficiency and electrification projects require preapproval.

approvalRequirements: Be a business customer of a participating Iowa Bright Energy Solutions utility
Use the current utility-specific application for an eligible business measure
Meet the applicable equipment, efficiency, installation, and customer requirements
Obtain preapproval before custom efficiency or custom electrification work
Submit invoices, equipment records, savings calculations, and other form-specific documentation
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Prescriptive rebates are generally likely for qualifying customers and equipment, while custom projects require advance approval and savings review.
reviews.evidenceText: The current directory lists 18 participating Iowa utilities. Member pages provide business rebate forms for multiple measure categories, with advance approval required for custom efficiency and electrification projects.

approvalRequirements: Be a business customer of a participating North Dakota Bright Energy Solutions utility
Use the current utility-specific application for an eligible business measure
Meet the applicable equipment, efficiency, installation, and customer requirements
Obtain preapproval before custom efficiency or custom electrification work
Submit invoices, equipment records, savings calculations, and other form-specific documentation
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Prescriptive rebates are generally likely for qualifying customers and equipment, while custom projects require advance approval and savings review.
reviews.evidenceText: The current directory lists five participating North Dakota utilities. Member pages provide business rebate forms for eligible measures and require preapproval for custom efficiency and electrification projects.

approvalRequirements: Place in service property that qualifies under the applicable current federal clean-energy investment credit rules
Establish and retain eligible tax basis and placed-in-service documentation
Satisfy prevailing-wage, apprenticeship, domestic-content, energy-community, or other rules for any enhanced percentage claimed
Claim the credit on Form 3468 with the applicable federal income-tax return
Complete pre-filing registration when using elective payment or credit transfer provisions
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: A properly documented statutory tax credit is generally available without competitive selection, but the target uses a legacy title and includes technologies that are not automatically qualifying property under current law.
reviews.evidenceText: The IRS states that the technology-neutral clean electricity investment credit applies to qualifying facilities and energy storage placed in service after 2024 and is claimed on Form 3468. Ordinary lighting or HVAC work does not qualify merely because it is energy efficient.

approvalRequirements: Be a current Butler Rural Electric Cooperative member and property owner
Select an eligible efficiency, heat-pump, or geothermal improvement and exclude ineligible new construction or distributed generation
Complete any required energy audit and submit the contractor bid before approval
Provide income, ownership, mortgage, insurance, and other credit documentation
Receive written loan and project approval before any work begins
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The cooperative offers defined low-interest financing, but approval depends on membership, project eligibility, credit documentation, property conditions, and approval before installation.
reviews.evidenceText: The current loan page requires cooperative membership and ownership, an eligible project, contractor bid and applicable audit, credit and property documentation, and approval before work. Loans are subject to financing review and stated exclusions.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Butler Rural Electric Cooperative homeowner-member
Contact the cooperative before heat-pump or geothermal installation and use the required participating or qualified contractor
Install equipment meeting current efficiency, building-age, service, and system-design requirements
Avoid excluded distributed-generation, net-metering, or nonqualifying system configurations
Submit the current application and supporting purchase or installation documentation within the applicable period
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current rebates use published amounts and are likely for compliant member installations, although advance contact, contractor and technical rules, funding, and continued-service conditions apply.
reviews.evidenceText: Current cooperative pages require advance contact and qualified contractors for heat-pump and geothermal systems and list technical and service conditions. The 2026 thermostat rebate is limited by cost, funding, and product requirements. A standalone furnace rebate is not shown.

approvalRequirements: Use an eligible commercial, industrial, agricultural, nonprofit, or qualifying multifamily property in a participating Colorado county
Submit the project for Colorado C-PACE prequalification and independent technical and financial review
Be current on property taxes and assessments and have no disqualifying bankruptcy or mortgage default
Obtain mortgage-holder consent and select a qualified private capital provider
Satisfy private underwriting and complete program closing and assessment-recording documents
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: C-PACE can finance eligible projects, but access depends on property and county eligibility, technical review, mortgage consent, private-capital underwriting, and successful closing rather than an automatic public award.
reviews.evidenceText: The current program offers private C-PACE financing after property and county qualification, technical and financial review, current tax and mortgage status, mortgage-holder consent, capital-provider underwriting, and program closing.

approvalRequirements: Use a qualifying commercial property in a Maine municipality participating in C-PACE
Propose a qualifying energy project and select a registered capital provider
Submit the Efficiency Maine application, required checklist documents, and nonrefundable application fee
Provide mortgage-lender consent and all required assessment, financing, and property documentation
Respond to requests for additional information or cure an incomplete or nonstandard submission within the permitted review process
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Projects require explicit Efficiency Maine approval and private financing arrangements; approval is possible for complete qualifying submissions but is not automatic.
reviews.evidenceText: The current C-PACE page states that every project must be approved by Efficiency Maine and requires a participating municipality, qualifying property and project, a registered capital provider, a complete application and fee, lender consent, and closing documentation.
